criteria: Uses a complete, correctly ordered interview structure (opening, information-gathering, objectives, advice, closing) within a realistic time budget
Uses predominantly open questions, narrows appropriately, and reflects back to check understanding
Distinguishes the client's stated request from their underlying objective and records it explicitly
Produces an attendance note that is accurate, complete, third-person, and usable by another fee-earner without further questioning the client
S01_INT_Core.pass_threshold: Meets the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) for interviewing: a controlled, client-focused structure; effective open and closed questioning; correctly identified objectives; and an attendance note a supervising solicitor could act on without re-interviewing the client.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, client interview and attendance note station

criteria: Applies the fixed interview structure correctly while adapting content and tone to the specific practice-area context
Uses context-appropriate open questioning and identifies risks/sensitivities specific to that context (e.g. privilege, capacity, urgency)
Correctly distinguishes the client's stated request from their real objective in that context
Produces a context-accurate, complete attendance note including any flagged next steps or risks
S02_INT_Worked_Scenarios.pass_threshold: Interview structure and questioning technique transfer correctly to each context; the client's context-specific objective is correctly identified; each attendance note reflects the real content and conventions of that practice area.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, client interview and attendance note station across practice contexts
source.reference: sqe.sra.org.uk SQE2 specification, Annex 1 (Criminal Practice, Dispute Resolution, Property Practice, Wills and Administration, Business Law and Practice)

criteria: Submission has a clear, logical, front-loaded structure with a stated proposition, ordered points, and a precise requested order
Addresses the opposing party's strongest point rather than ignoring it
Demonstrates correct question form for the task (open/non-leading in chief, closed/leading in cross)
Uses correct forms of address, bundle references, and courtroom conduct throughout, within time
S03_ADV_Core.pass_threshold: Meets the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) for advocacy: a clear, logical, persuasive structure; questioning technique matching examination-in-chief or cross-examination as required; and conduct and etiquette appropriate to the tribunal, under the real 45-minute preparation and 15-minute presentation timing.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, advocacy station

criteria: Correctly identifies the tribunal, the applicable test/procedure, and uses context-appropriate forms of address
Structures the submission with a front-loaded proposition and points in descending strength, supported by facts/authority
Directly addresses the strongest point against the client rather than ignoring it
Maintains courteous, controlled conduct and finishes within the time allowed
S04_ADV_Worked_Scenarios.pass_threshold: Submission structure and questioning technique are applied correctly to the specific hearing type in each context; the tribunal and etiquette for that context are correctly identified; the strongest point against the client is addressed, not avoided.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, advocacy station across practice contexts
source.reference: sqe.sra.org.uk SQE2 specification, Annex 1 (Criminal Practice, Dispute Resolution, Property Practice, Wills and Administration, Business Law and Practice)

criteria: Correctly identifies the central legal issues as questions, without drowning them in side issues
Builds an accurate chronology and explicitly flags factual conflicts between documents
Identifies genuine, decisive gaps and states assumptions clearly rather than guessing silently
Produces a structured, client-focused report ending in an explicit, reasoned recommendation
S05_CMA_Core.pass_threshold: Meets the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) for case and matter analysis: correctly identifies the legal issues and relevant facts from an unfamiliar bundle within the 60-minute limit, flags genuine gaps, and produces a structured, client-focused report with a supported recommendation.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, case and matter analysis station (60-minute computer-based written task)

criteria: Spots the issues, facts and gaps that are actually typical/decisive for that specific practice area, not a generic list
Builds an accurate chronology and flags conflicts or missing evidence specific to the context
Distinguishes decisive gaps from minor ones and states assumptions where facts are missing
Recommendation is explicit, realistic, and weighs the client's practical position, not just legal merits
S06_CMA_Worked_Scenarios.pass_threshold: The analysis method (issues, facts/conflicts, gaps, options, recommendation) is applied accurately to bundle content typical of each context, with issues and gaps specific to that area of law correctly spotted.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, case and matter analysis station across practice contexts

criteria: Frames a precise, answerable research question from a vague or general instruction
Correctly identifies and prioritises which provided source(s) actually answer the framed question
Applies the law found to the client's specific facts with reasoning, not just a restatement of the source
Presents a structured, accurately referenced answer with a clear final conclusion
S07_RES_Core.pass_threshold: Meets the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) for legal research: frames a precise, answerable question, identifies and uses relevant sources and information provided, applies the law correctly to the facts, and presents a clearly referenced answer within the 60-minute limit.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, legal research station (60-minute computer-based written task)

criteria: Frames a precise research question specific to the practice-area facts given
Identifies and correctly uses source material typical of that practice area
Applies the source accurately to the facts with clear reasoning, addressing genuine counter-arguments
Presents a properly referenced answer ending in an explicit, usable conclusion
S08_RES_Worked_Scenarios.pass_threshold: The research method is applied accurately to a realistic instruction in each context, using materials typical of that area (guidelines, procedural rules, statutory provisions, case authority) correctly identified, applied and referenced.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, legal research station across practice contexts
source.reference: sqe.sra.org.uk SQE2 specification, Annex 1 (Criminal Practice, Dispute Resolution, Property Practice, Wills and Administration, Business Law and Practice)

criteria: Uses clear, precise, concise language matched correctly to the intended reader
Selects and correctly structures the right document type for the task (attendance note, file note, letter of advice, or third-party correspondence)
States the substantive conclusion/advice clearly and early, not buried or left implicit
Content is accurate to the facts given, with appropriate next steps and no unsupported claims
S09_WRI_Core.pass_threshold: Meets the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) for legal writing: clear, precise, concise and acceptable language for the intended reader; correct document type and structure; and accurate content, within the 30-minute limit.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, legal writing station (30-minute computer-based written task)

criteria: Selects the right document type and structure for the reader and purpose in that context
Leads with a clear conclusion/recommendation appropriate to that practice area's likely client concerns
Content is accurate to the scenario facts, with technical terms explained where the reader would need it
Register and tone are appropriately matched to the named reader (anxious individual client vs. formal third party vs. business client)
S10_WRI_Worked_Scenarios.pass_threshold: The correct document type is produced with content accurate to the practice-area facts, clear conclusions, and register appropriate to the named reader in each context.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, legal writing station across practice contexts
source.reference: sqe.sra.org.uk SQE2 specification, Annex 1 (Criminal Practice, Dispute Resolution, Property Practice, Wills and Administration, Business Law and Practice)

criteria: Drafts precisely to the instructions given, adding nothing and omitting nothing, with gaps flagged rather than invented
Uses plain English and avoids unnecessary archaic drafting language
Defined terms and cross-references are used correctly and consistently throughout
The document/clause is unambiguous and includes any consequence the instruction implies (what happens if the obligation is not met)
S11_DRA_Core.pass_threshold: Meets the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) for legal drafting: a document or clause that is legally correct, precise, unambiguous, and follows the instructions given, within the 45-minute limit.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, legal drafting station (45-minute computer-based written task)

criteria: Uses the document convention/format typical of that practice area correctly (numbered particulars, resolution format, will clause language, notice format)
Drafts precisely to the instructions given, with any gap flagged rather than invented
Clause/document is unambiguous, with defined terms and consequences stated where implied by the instruction
Content is accurate and consistent with the underlying scenario facts from earlier stages
S12_DRA_Worked_Scenarios.pass_threshold: The document or clause is drafted precisely to instructions with content and format typical of that practice area, unambiguous, and with any gap in the instructions flagged rather than filled by invention.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, legal drafting station across practice contexts
source.reference: sqe.sra.org.uk SQE2 specification, Annex 1 (Criminal Practice, Dispute Resolution, Property Practice, Wills and Administration, Business Law and Practice)

criteria: Performance across all six skills is consistent with the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3), not just strong on some skills and weak on others
Oral skills (interviewing, advocacy) show correct structure, technique and courtroom/interview conduct under live or recorded, timed conditions
Written skills (case analysis, research, writing, drafting) show correct method and produce an accurate, usable, client-focused document or analysis under timed conditions
Performance holds up when skills are applied to an unfamiliar practice-area context, not only the ones most recently practised
Every one of the five practice-area contexts has been tested successfully for at least one skill before the exam is recorded as passed
exam_rubric.pass_threshold: A pass requires performance consistent with the SQE2 Threshold Standard (Level 3) across all six skills and, cumulatively, across all five practice-area contexts sampled, marked on the SRA's six-point A-F scale with skill and application of law weighted equally. The SRA does not publish a fixed raw mark boundary; it sets the standard per sitting via its standard-setting process.

source.document: SRA SQE2 Assessment Specification, full assessment structure (oral and written sittings)

source_notes: The old build had zero itemisation: curriculum_map.json carried only a broad topic index with no _syllabus_items, so no prior source_urls/source_notes existed to carry over.

This build itemises all six SQE2 skills (client interviewing, advocacy, case and matter analysis, legal research, legal writing, legal drafting) crossed with the five practice-area contexts named in the brief (Criminal Practice, Dispute Resolution, Property Practice, Wills and Intestacy/Probate Administration and Practice, Business Organisations Rules and Procedures), for the first time.

Timings and formats per skill (e.g. interview 25 minutes oral + 25 minutes attendance note; advocacy 45 minutes prep + 15 minutes presentation; case analysis/legal research 60 minutes each; legal writing 30 minutes; legal drafting 45 minutes) and the oral/written sitting structure (2 half-days oral, 3 half-days written) were confirmed from the live SQE2 specification page.

The exact skill-to-context pairing on any one candidate's sitting is not fixed by the SRA and varies between administrations, subject to its published principle that each skill is assessed at least twice across the assessment; the EXAM block reflects that published principle rather than inventing a fixed permutation.
